# Independent audit: common-slice quantiles and cross-direction tails

Source: `candidate 5dd0d34dec315bd7`.
Full proof audited PASS with no correction required. This is an actual
one-body cross-direction inequality, not a combination of independently
chosen marginal extremizers. The accompanying independent exact checker
uses actual thin triangles and trapezoids, including positive and negative
selector slopes.

## 1. Selector existence and coordinate width

The projection interval [l,h] has l<h because A is full dimensional.
Compactness supplies actual endpoint points. Their connecting segment
belongs to A by convexity and gives an affine selector X(t) on every
section. Its second coordinate is exactly Y(t)=-t-X(t). No claim that
section centers themselves move affinely is used.

On each section t=-x-y, the x coordinates form an interval of length
ell(t)<=W. The selected point lies in that interval, so its distance
from any x coordinate is <=W. The same bound holds for y because
y=-t-x within the section. This is a coordinate interval width, not a
Euclidean diagonal-section length or a half-width. The map
(t,x)->(x,-t-x) has determinant +1, so integrating ell(t) in t gives
the original area exactly; no missing sqrt(2) coarea factor occurs.
Other canonical pairs of normals give determinant of absolute value one.

## 2. The lower quantile and both selector slopes

Uniform area induces an atom-free distribution in t. Every section at
an interior level has positive length, so its cumulative distribution
is continuous and strictly increasing there. Thus p=v/a in (0,1/2)
has a unique interior lower quantile t_p.

If X has nonpositive slope and X(t_p)>-1+W, continuity supplies some
t_p+epsilon<h where this inequality still holds. Monotonicity then
makes X(t)>-1+W for every t below that value. Every point in those
sections is captured by x>=-1, giving area >pa=v and contradicting
u<=v. This correctly handles zero slope as well.

If X has positive slope and X(t_p)>=-1+W, every section strictly
above t_p is wholly captured by x>=-1. Its area is (1-p)a>pa,
again impossible. Thus the weaker conclusion X(t_p)<=-1+W always
holds, with strictness in this positive-slope case. The identical
argument for Y uses its own cap mass v=pa. Adding yields
t_p>=2-2W and therefore F_A(2-2W)<=v for the UNNORMALIZED area CDF.
The source's use of normalized F is equivalent. Equality and zero
slopes are included; no choice of quantile orientation is reversed.

## 3. Width and strip constants

Interval-section interpolation makes ell concave. The triangular
lower envelope from zero endpoint heights to a maximal or supremizing
height W gives a>=W(h-l)/2, even when the maximum occurs at an endpoint.
If t=-1 is proper, l<-1<h, so H=h+1>0 and h-l>H, giving
W<=2a/(h-l)<2a/H.

The strip between levels 2-2W and 2 has t-length 2W and coordinate
width at most W. Its area is at most 2W^2, including cases where
part of the strip lies beyond the actual projection. Together with
the quantile estimate and the area-null boundary lines, this proves

    tau_A(2)>=a-v-2W^2>=a-v-8a^2/H^2.

The final stated weak inequality is valid; the width comparison actually
makes its substitution strict. There is no assumption that area alone
controls an arbitrary Euclidean diameter.

## 4. Actual lower-cap interpolation and the quadratic

In the final section, e=a-w>0 is the actual lower-cap area at -1,
and h>2 makes 2 an interior level between -1 and h. Lower caps have
concave area square root by their actual Minkowski inclusion and ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski. At the full upper level h the lower-cap area is a.
The interpolation weight is exactly (2+1)/(h+1)=3/H, so

    sqrt(F_A(2)) >= sqrt(e)+(3/H)(sqrt(a)-sqrt(e)).

The strip estimate gives F_A(2)<=v+8a^2/H^2. Multiplying by H>0
and squaring NONNEGATIVE sides gives precisely

    (v-e)H^2 -6sqrt(e)(sqrt(a)-sqrt(e))H
        +8a^2 -9(sqrt(a)-sqrt(e))^2 >=0.

Every constant and sign matches. Here w>0 and e<a, so Delta>0.
If v<=e and 8a^2<9Delta^2 the constant term is strictly negative
and the other two terms are nonpositive; hence the claimed impossible
parameter regime follows for every allowed H.

## 5. Scope

The condition v<a/2 is essential to the positive-slope argument and
is retained. The lemma permits u=0; only v must be positive. When
used in the all-proper cap application, that stronger positivity
comes from the application, not from an unstated requirement here.
All quantities concern the SAME actual planar body, and all sections
and endpoint selector points belong to it. No affine-width or triangle
assumption enters the proof. This does not by itself prove any full
mixed-depth bound or the cited separate shifted-cover estimate.

Verifier: `supporting computation verify_affine_selector_tail_audit_slab_recovery.py`.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
